verdicts.note: Upheld with a caveat: the pamphlet also criticizes cuts to K-12 programs (Running Start, Transitional Kindergarten), and the site calls for full state funding of special education and transportation. Those are priorities inside the budget, not calls to expand it, and repeated 'reduce spending' / 'cut wasteful spending' / 'budgets tied to results' statements support -2.
Explicit pledges to 'defend sex-based sports' and protect locker-room and overnight-travel privacy match the pole_a description. There is no abortion evidence, so medium (not high) is right.

Upheld at the edge: the site has a 'Support Parental Rights' plank pledging to defend parents' right to be informed, provide meaningful access to curriculum information, and 'push back on policies that cut parents out of decisions'. It names no specific measure (I-2081, I-1, opt-outs, health-service notification), so -1 would also be defensible; medium confidence already reflects a single statement.

Roll calls verified (S5 live, S10-S13 cache): nay on ESSB 6346 House final passage (2026-03-09, 51-46) and nay on House final passage of ESSB 5801, ESHB 2081, ESSB 5813 and ESSB 5814. His 'more than simply raising taxes on the wealthy' wording (S3) concedes some role for taxing the wealthy, so -1 rather than -2 is right; several independent votes support high.

The cited source (S6, ESHB 1296 roll calls) shows more than the final-passage yea. On 2025-03-12 Richards voted yea on ten Republican floor amendments that failed about 42-52, each restoring or adding I-2081 rights: Caldier/Valdez 448 (notice of school-arranged medical treatment needing follow-up care), Steele 420 (prior notice of medical services), Walsh 396 (notice of services with financial impact), Marshall 435 and 442 (medical/health and mental-health counseling records made inspectable), Couture 444 (immediate notice when a child is removed from campus, including to a shelter or host home), Ley 437 (child under 18 may not authorize own excused absences), Burnett 382 (monthly evening/weekend curriculum review), Keaton 383 (staff to support implementing the parents' bill of rights) and Schmidt 384 (private right of action). Amendment texts are from lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov, cached in data/.cache/leg/amd/. He then voted yea at third reading and on final passage. The record is mixed, which is what 0 means. The dossier's Parents and schools section should add these amendment votes so the score is dossier-supported.
